title: What It's Like To Be Eaten By A Carnivorous Plant

title_pattern.template: What It's Like To Be [killed/processed] By A [Surprising Agent]
title_pattern.type: second-person morbid POV / 'what it feels like' experiential explainer
title_pattern.notes: Puts the viewer inside the victim's body. Morbid curiosity + harmless cartoon framing. No number in title even though the video is a countdown list (5 trap types); the list is the structure, the POV is the promise. Plain sentence case, no caps-lock or emoji.

thumbnail.composition: Three-subject lineup on pure white: left a yellow pitcher plant with the dog mascot's head poking out (calm, smiling); centre a giant Venus flytrap mid-bite on the stick-figure man, his head hanging out sideways with streaming tears; right a sundew tentacle coiled around a second terrified stick figure. Each subject fills most of the frame height; no empty space.
thumbnail.colours: White background, saturated flat lime/kelly green plants, one yellow pitcher, pink tongue/teeth accents, thick black outlines, pink dotted glue halo on the sundew. 3-4 flat colours total.
thumbnail.subject_scale_contrast: Plants drawn huge relative to the humans (human head = size of the trap mouth), inverting normal scale - that is the whole concept in one image. Mascot's happy face contrasts with the victims' horror faces.
thumbnail.why_it_works: Reads instantly at phone size: thick outlines, flat colour, no text. Shows three different 'death methods' as a menu, promising variety. Comedic suffering (tears, panic) on a cute art style = safe morbid curiosity. Recognisable channel mascot on the left builds brand recall.

hook.verbatim_0_10s: Hello bug-sized men. Have you ever wondered what it's like to be eaten by a carnivorous plant? No? Well, let's find out. Number five, pitcher plant.
hook.visual_0_8s: Dog mascot zaps a stick-figure man with a star wand (0s), man shrinks to bug size next to tiny insects (2-4s), then a grey spotlight stage shows the shrunk man cowering surrounded by all the plants of the video - flytraps, sundews, pitchers (6s). Hard cut to black 'NUMBER 5' card at 8s.
hook.device: Direct-address with a joke ('Hello bug-sized men'), rhetorical question + comedic 'No? Well, let's find out' deflation, instant transformation gag that sets up the POV premise, a one-frame preview of every threat, then immediate countdown start. Zero intro, no channel branding; content begins at 8s.

beats.summary: Mascot shrinks the viewer-avatar to bug size; asks what being eaten by a carnivorous plant is like; preview of all plants.
NUMBER 5 black card, then PITCHER PLANTS title card with a cartoon pitcher; 'Let me out!' gag line.
Second-person narrative: lured by nectar scent, slurping on waxy rim, slipping, falling into fluid, can't climb waxy walls, drowning, digested alive.
Mascot answers 'Why must you do this?': poor swampy soil, plant gets nitrogen/phosphorus/magnesium from prey; diet mostly bugs but some eat frogs and rats. 'Subscribe, dude' throwaway.
Toilet-shaped pitcher (Nepenthes lowii): tree shrews eat nectar from the lid and poop into the bowl - 'this pitcher plant eats poop'.
Cobra lily: climbing the forked tongue with increasing nectar, entering a glowing dome, false windows, confusion, sliding deeper, eaten by midge larvae and bacteria into nutrient soup.
'If you don't want to be eaten by my pet plant, boop the like button'; recap that pitchers are first of five; 'Number four, bladderwort'.

beats.beat_type: list item: setup + POV + mechanism + gore
beats.summary: Bladderwort: pretty flowers above, murder below; swimming happily then sudden black darkness; mechanism of negative-pressure bladder trapdoor and trigger hairs (pee joke); diet; staged digestion head, body, legs into soup.

NUMBER 3 card, STICKY-LEAVED PLANTS; sundew nectar laced with glue ('it's a wrap, literally'), tentacles curl in, suffocation via clogged breathing holes, dissolved to skeleton; 'hugged to death sounds nice'; butterwort variant with butter-and-toast gag.
Rhododendron macrosepalum traps, mirid bug stabs you with its face and poops the soup for the plant; puzzle 'why doesn't it catch this bug?' answered: thick grease coating.
NUMBER 2 card; rolling in dirt, find tunnel ('treasure?'), one-way hairs, forced deeper, digestive chamber, slow death; diet protozoans/mites/annelids; plant needn't lure, critters walk in.

'I bet you've all been waiting for this one'; diet pie chart myth-bust (1/3 ants, 1/3 spiders, ~5% flyers); four-adaptation grid filled one by one: red colour + scent, two-touch trigger hairs (7-ish snaps, raindrop), lashes let small prey escape, repeated triggering before sealing; airtight clamp, suffocation, dissolved over days to a skeleton.
'So many exciting ways to be eaten. Now watch this one next, or else.' Pet piranha plant + spiked ball threat gag; 'See you next time.'

pacing.notes: Narration is near-continuous (~158 wpm, conversational). Visual changes roughly every 2-5 s; many 'shots' are the same static scene with a sprite swapped (expression change, prop appears), so perceived pace is faster than the cut count. Presenter cutaways to the dog on white every ~10-20 s act as breathers and cover fact-delivery lines. Each list item is ~60-100 s; items run setup -> POV death -> mechanism/fact -> gore payoff -> dog joke.

art_style.palette: Pure white background (#FFFFFF) dominant; flat saturated greens (#22DD22-ish lime, mint #8EF58E for interiors), yellow #FFE600, orange #F4A020, hot pink #E85A9A / magenta #A8326A, pale cyan #E6FFFF for water, red collar accent. Black #000 outlines 3-5 px.
art_style.characters: Dog mascot: white, floppy ears, red collar, stick legs, ~1/3 frame height, always on the right third on presenter shots. Victim: blank round-head stick figure with dot eyes - expressions done purely by eyes/mouth.
art_style.typography: Rounded hand-drawn all-caps display font for titles (black on white), clean bold sans for photo captions, italic grey Latin names under captions. Black full-frame 'NUMBER N' cards in white rounded font.
art_style.real_media: Real photos and credited YouTube clips appear in rounded-corner frames with a soft drop shadow, always paired with the dog presenter - used for credibility on each new species.

techniques_worth_copying: Second-person 'you' POV narration ('your insect brain is lured in...') turns a list of facts into a survival story per item.
Shrink-the-viewer premise in the first 2 seconds sets a single consistent avatar for the whole video.

Countdown list with black 'NUMBER N' cards + bespoke animated title card per category; saves the most famous item (Venus flytrap) for last and calls it out ('I bet you've all been waiting for this one').
Every item ends on a visual payoff: soup, mush, skeleton - consistent 'death reveal' gives a rhythm viewers anticipate.
Presenter cutaways (mascot on white, right third) for exposition lines; free to animate cheaply and break up dense facts.
Fact delivered as visual metaphor: dinner cloche for diet, chef with NECTAR/GLUE bottles, flytrap at a dinner table with an energy meter, FREE COOKIES sign on the trap tunnel.
Four-circle progress grid to count adaptations - tells the viewer how much is left.
Pie chart myth-bust (flytraps barely eat flies) - counterintuitive stat as a mini-hook inside the climax.
Scale inversion: tiny human vs giant plant in wides, then extreme close-ups of the face for emotion.
Smash cut to pure black for sudden capture (bladderwort) - silence/darkness as a jump scare.
Comic deflation lines ('No? Well, let's find out', 'A wholesome symbiotic relationship', 'being hugged to death sounds nice').
Mid-roll CTA disguised as a threat gag ('if you don't want to be eaten by my pet plant, boop the like button') and outro 'watch this one next, or else'.
Real photo/clip inserts with credit lines for every species keep it educational and trustworthy.
Descriptive chapters in the description (one per plant) for search and retention.

code_only_remake_needs.feasibility: High. Everything except the real photos/clips is flat vector art on white with hard cuts and simple sprite swaps - ideal for Remotion + SVG.
assets: Mascot presenter SVG with 4-6 poses (idle, point, arms out, hold-prop, shocked) and a blink/mouth flap rig.
Stick-figure avatar SVG with swappable eyes/mouth (happy, ?, shocked, crying, X-eyes, $-eyes) and limb poses (walk, crawl, swim, lick, fall).
Per-subject environment SVGs: giant trap exteriors, cross-sections, interiors with radial gradients, top-down pools.
Prop/icon library: cloche, toilet, chef hat, bottles, pie chart, progress circles, insects, skeleton, ghost, spiked ball.
Photo replacement: real reference photos can't be reused; substitute public-domain/CC images with credits, or draw stylised 'specimen card' illustrations in SVG.
components: TitleCard (display font heading + animated hero illustration).
PresenterShot (mascot right third + left slot for photo card / text list / prop).
PhotoCard (rounded frame, drop shadow, caption + italic Latin name + optional credit line).
ScentRibbon (animated wavy SVG path from source to nose).
CrossSection scene with fluid level animation and progressive dissolve (mask/opacity/colour lerp to orange soup, then skeleton swap).
PieChartBuild and ProgressGrid (N circles filling one by one).
Smash-to-black cut and simple scale-jump 'zoom' cuts (no camera moves needed beyond occasional push-in).
code_only_remake_needs.audio_timing: Local TTS narration at ~155-160 wpm with a casual, deadpan tone; word-level timestamps to drive sprite swaps every 2-4 s; short character vocal stingers ('Let me out!', 'No, please', 'o no') as separate TTS lines with a different voice/pitch.
code_only_remake_needs.script: Write original: pick a different 'what it's like to be X by Y' subject, 5-item countdown, each item = lure -> trap -> failed escape -> mechanism fact -> death payoff -> mascot joke; ~1300-1400 words for ~8.5 min.
